title: Content: routine & block library (SPEC §7)
description:
Curated workout content on top of the MVP schema — all pure data files designed WITH the owner; deliberately no in-app editor UI (SPEC §2). Children: GIF fetch tooling + quota ledger, warm-up/cooldown blocks, two dumbbell strength routines, physio rehab blocks (hard-gated on the MVP phone test ft-mvp-ow6.11), and 40+ min sessions composed from blocks.

## Success Criteria
- Every shipped block/routine validates against the schema, has a GIF (or deliberate text card) per interval, and appears in the picker with zero app-code changes.
- Physio blocks carry citations from reputable sources.
- All child beads closed.
acceptance_criteria: all shipped content validates, renders, and is picker-visible with zero code changes; physio blocks cite sources; all children closed

title: GIF fetch script + committed quota ledger (SPEC §6.10)
description:
node scripts/fetch-gifs.mjs <exerciseId...> (SPEC §6.10, §4): reads WORKOUTX_KEY from env (never committed — public repo), downloads missing GIFs to data/gifs/, skips files already present, paces under 30 req/min, records the X-Quota-Remaining response header, and appends {date, ids, calls, quotaRemaining} to a committed ledger (data/quota-ledger.json). Treat 503 'watermarked GIF unavailable' (known: ids 5202, 5204) as skip-and-report so a substitute can be chosen — never retry a 503 into the quota. ~330 of 500 monthly calls remain as of 2026-08-10; batch fetches per design session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running twice for the same ids costs zero API calls the second time.
- Ledger matches the API's reported quota drift.
- A 503 id is skipped with a clear report and no retries.
acceptance_criteria: second run for same ids costs zero calls; ledger matches API quota drift; 503 ids skip with report, no retry

title: Warm-up & cooldown blocks (designed with owner)
description:
2-3 reusable ~5-min blocks designed WITH the owner (interactive session, not solo): a general dynamic warm-up, a dumbbell-session warm-up, a stretch cooldown. Pick candidates from data/exercises/catalog_full.json (filter lists in data/exercises/), fetch GIFs via ft-content-e0q.1. These become the prefix/suffix for 40+ min composed sessions (ft-content-e0q.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Blocks validate against the schema; every interval has a GIF; owner signed off on the exercise selection.
acceptance_criteria: blocks validate; every interval has a GIF; owner signed off on selection

description:
Two 20-30 min dumbbell sessions designed WITH the owner (e.g. full-body A/B), structured as reusable blocks. Strength pacing differs from HIIT — longer work, longer rest — and the schema's per-interval seconds must express it. The owner's dumbbells are a light set (the MadFit video used 2x10 lb) — choose exercises accordingly (SPEC §8).

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Physio: owner interview, reputable-source research, rehab/mobility blocks with citations. HARD RULE: not before MVP phone test
description:

Then: run a focused interview on problem areas; research reputable physio sources (professional bodies, peer-reviewed material, physiotherapy clinics — not fitness-blog sludge); build 1-2 rehab/mobility blocks per problem area with citations kept in each block file's notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Compose 40+ min sessions from blocks (pure data)
description:
Pure data: named routines composing existing blocks — warm-up + MadFit + cooldown; warm-up + strength + core + cooldown (SPEC §2: 40+ min sessions). Zero new app code if the schema (ft-mvp-ow6.1) held up — this bead doubles as the schema's real-world composition test.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Implement four integrated routines (v2) as app data — W1-W4 super workouts
description:
Implement the four integrated "super workout" routines as installable app data so the owner can test them on his phone.

CANONICAL SPEC: docs/research/draft-routines-v2.md — exact per-interval exercise lists, sides, coach cues, RPE targets, and global safety rules for W1 "Iron Roots" (30×40/20), W2 "Silk Coils" (30×40/20), W3 "Dragon Longform" (45×40/20), W4 "Crane Longform" (45×40/20). Do not re-derive intervals from anywhere else; v2 already incorporates the oracle design review (docs/research/oracle-routine-review.md) over the five-source evidence base (docs/research/synthesis.md; profile in docs/research/interview.md).

Scope:
1. Map every v2 exercise to the WorkoutX catalog (data/exercises/catalog_full.json) by name/target; record the mapping (exerciseId or none) per interval.
2. GIFs: reuse the 27 already in data/gifs/ where they match; fetch missing ones with the ft-content-e0q.1 script (check the quota ledger first; ~330 calls/month available as of 2026-08-10; 503 ids = skip and substitute). Many physio/mobility/kick stations will have NO catalog match — use the text-card path (established for MadFit interval 2) with the coach cue as the card body; a text card is a deliberate choice, not a failure.
3. Write the four routine JSONs per data/SCHEMA.md (blocks where reuse is natural — e.g. the shared warm-up ramp and rehab-spine stations — inline intervals otherwise). Encode coachNotes: tempo, RPE target, and the safety cues from v2's global rules (toe-safe regression, planted feet, neutral grip, calf 3-1-3).
4. Timer semantics: sessions must run exactly 30:00/45:00 — the final 20 s rest is kept (v2 header; verify engine behavior, fix or file if it stops after last work interval).
5. Register all four in the picker (data/content-index.json or current mechanism) — zero app-code changes expected; if code changes ARE needed, that is a schema/picker bug to file separately.
6. Validate: node scripts/validate.mjs over all routine files passes; every interval renders either a GIF or a text card.

Out of scope: the habit-anchored Achilles dosing card (docs, not app data); the dedicated clinic routine (future); qigong (skipped by owner decision 2026-08-10).

Done means: all four routines validate, appear in the picker, and are runnable end-to-end on the deployed PWA so the owner can try them ASAP.
acceptance_criteria: all four routines validate, appear in the picker with zero app-code changes, every interval shows a GIF or deliberate text card with cues, and each runs exactly 30:00/45:00 end-to-end on the deployed PWA

title: MVP: run the MadFit session on the owner's phone (SPEC §7)
description:
Everything needed for the owner to complete one real MadFit 30-min HIIT session on their phone, with their own music playing uninterrupted in the background. Children cover: routine/block schema (the contract), PWA shell, interval engine, workout screen, WebAudio cues, voice announcements, wake lock, routine picker, MadFit port + GIF audit, GitHub Pages deploy + real-phone test, and history/streaks. Canonical spec: docs/SPEC.md (product decisions §2, architecture §6, plan §7).

## Success Criteria
- ft-mvp-ow6.11's real-phone test passed: one full MadFit workout completed on the owner's phone via the deployed PWA, background music never interrupted.
- All child beads closed.
acceptance_criteria: one real MadFit workout completed on the owner's phone via the deployed PWA; all children closed

title: Routine & block schema + validator; convert MadFit JSON (SPEC §6.1)
description:
The contract everything else depends on — engine, picker, and all future content. Block = named, reusable ordered list of intervals {exerciseId, displayName, gif, workSeconds, restSeconds, side?, coachNote?}. Routine = metadata {title, equipment, estDuration} + ordered list of block refs and/or inline intervals. Must support per-side exercises, combo intervals (two movements alternated in one interval — MadFit #12/#22/#23), and blocks shared across routines. Deliverables: data/SCHEMA.md documenting every field; a dependency-free validator (node scripts/validate.mjs data/routines/*.json); convert data/routines/madfit-30min-hiit.json (interim shape — see its notes field) to the final schema as the reference example.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Validator passes on the converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures (missing gif ref, zero/negative seconds, unknown block ref, invalid side) — keep the fixtures in the repo as the validator's test suite.
- Schema expresses per-side exercises, combo intervals, and cross-routine block reuse.
- data/SCHEMA.md documents every field, its optionality, and units.
acceptance_criteria: validator passes on converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures; schema covers per-side, combo, and cross-routine block reuse; SCHEMA.md complete
close_reason: Delivered schema v1, reusable block composition, converted 30-interval MadFit routine, dependency-free validator, and fixtures. Verified: validator + fixture tests pass; migration invariants preserve 30:00 duration and all exercise/GIF refs; UBS exits 0.

title: Port MadFit to final schema + GIF audit: 3 loose matches + missing #2 (SPEC §7)
description:
Convert the mapped MadFit data (30 intervals, 27 GIFs; interim JSON at data/routines/madfit-30min-hiit.json) to the final ft-mvp-ow6.1 schema. Audit the weak visuals: the 3 loose matches — #16 commandos (0664 Push-up To Side Plank), #19 plank pull-throughs (0521 KB Alternating Renegade Row), #27 standing DB crunch (1005 Band Standing Crunch) — plus #2 bum kicks (no catalog match). For each: keep, substitute a better catalog GIF (fetch via ft-content-e0q.1 tooling; note catalog id 5204 'commando' returns 503 watermarked-unavailable on the free plan, SPEC §4), or use a text-only card where a GIF would mislead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Validator passes; all 30 intervals show a sensible visual; no broken GIF refs.
- Each of the 4 audited intervals has its decision recorded in coachNote or routine notes.
acceptance_criteria: validator passes; all 30 intervals show sensible visuals with no broken refs; 4 audited intervals carry recorded decisions
close_reason: MadFit is on schema v1; validator expands all 30 intervals with no broken GIF refs. Audited #2/#16/#19/#27 now record explicit text-card or retained-GIF decisions in coachNote.

title: Workout history + streaks: localStorage log, month calendar (SPEC §6.9)
description:

title: Interval engine: timestamp-anchored state machine (SPEC §6.3)
description:
Pure JS state machine (idle/work/rest/paused/done) as a standalone module with no DOM access (SPEC §6.3). Timing is timestamp-anchored: compute remaining time from clock deltas, never accumulate setInterval ticks. Controls: pause/resume, skip forward/back one interval, restart. Emits tick, intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, countdown321; UI and audio are subscribers only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests (node --test, injected fake clock, zero deps) cover: every state transition, pause/resume across a work→rest boundary, skip at first/last interval, restart, and recovery after a simulated 10s stall.
- A 30-interval run finishes within 1s of wall clock.
- Skip/pause/resume never desync display state from engine state.
acceptance_criteria: node --test suite passes (fake clock: transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, 10s stall); 30-interval run within 1s of wall clock
close_reason: Delivered pure timestamp-anchored idle/work/rest/paused/done engine with pause/resume, skip both directions, restart, and required events. node --test passes fake-clock transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, restart, 10s stall recovery, cue timing, and 30-minute wall-clock anchoring; UBS exits 0 after triage.

title: Workout screen UI, phone-first portrait dark (SPEC §6.4)
description:
Phone-first portrait dark UI (SPEC §6.4): big remaining-time display, current exercise GIF + name, next-up preview during rest, interval counter n/30, overall progress bar, pause/skip buttons sized for sweaty thumbs. Subscribes to engine events only — no timing logic in the UI layer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Full MadFit session runnable end-to-end on a phone without mis-taps.
- During rest, the NEXT exercise's GIF + name is shown (consistent with the voice announcement).
- Interval #2 (bum kicks — no GIF) renders its text-only card without layout breakage.
acceptance_criteria: full session runnable on phone without mis-taps; rest shows next-up preview; GIF-less intervals render a clean text card
notes: Workout UI is implemented. GIF clipping defect found during visual QA: intrinsic square grid items rendered 348px tall inside a 254px stage despite object-fit: contain. Fixed by constraining the grid row with minmax(0, 1fr) and allowing image min-height: 0. Playwright at 390x844 and 1024x900 confirms complete single and two-GIF interval renders with zero page/console errors. Bead remains open pending a full real-phone session/mis-tap check.

title: Audio cues via WebAudio that don't kill background music (SPEC §6.5)
description:
WebAudio-synthesized beeps only: 3-2-1 countdown, distinct work-start and rest-start tones, optional halfway tick (SPEC §6.5). NEVER an <audio> element or Media Session use — those pause/duck the user's Spotify/YT Music, and playing over the user's own music is this app's core differentiator. Create/resume the AudioContext on the Start tap (autoplay policy).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cues audible over playing Spotify on real Android Chrome AND real iOS Safari; music never pauses or ducks.
- Every engine cue event (countdown321, intervalStart work/rest, halfway) produces its distinct sound through a full session.
acceptance_criteria: cues audible over Spotify on real Android Chrome and iOS Safari with zero music pause/duck; all engine cue events sound correctly
notes: Implemented WebAudio-only synthesized cues for intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, and countdown321. AudioContext is created/resumed from the Start gesture; stale catch-up events are suppressed. Verified with 5 unit tests, full 15-test suite, PWA policy checks forbidding <audio>/Media Session, and a real Chromium browser unlock/start check at 390x844 with no page errors. Acceptance remains open pending Spotify mixing verification on real Android Chrome and iOS Safari through a full session.

title: Voice: pre-rendered FrankenTTS clips + SpeechSynthesis fallback (SPEC §6.6)
description:
DECIDED (SPEC §6.6): pre-render every phrase with FrankenTTS (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_tts — Rust Qwen3-TTS reimplementation, MIT code + Apache-2.0 weights) at CONTENT-BUILD time on the owner's 3090 box, ship small audio clips with the PWA, play via WebAudio. On-phone runtime FrankenTTS was evaluated and REJECTED: ~2 GB model, several GB RAM, desktop-only, 0.31x real time in WASM. The vocabulary is tiny and fixed (exercise names, 'go', 'rest', digits, 'left'/'right'), so clips are cheap. Deliverable includes a scripts/ tool that renders a routine's phrase list to clips. Fallback: browser SpeechSynthesis for any phrase lacking a clip — iOS requires a user-gesture unlock, so initialize speech on the Start tap. Behavior: announce next exercise (and side) during rest; 'go'/'rest' at boundaries; toggleable; queued so speech never overlaps the 3-2-1 beeps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Eyes-free MadFit session possible: every interval announced in time, sides included.
- All MadFit phrases have pre-rendered clips; the SpeechSynthesis fallback demonstrably speaks a deliberately clip-less phrase on iOS after the Start-tap unlock.
- Speech never overlaps countdown beeps.
acceptance_criteria: eyes-free session works; all MadFit phrases pre-rendered; fallback speaks clip-less phrases on iOS post-unlock; speech never overlaps beeps

title: Wake lock + ergonomics (SPEC §6.7)
description:
Screen Wake Lock API with re-acquire on visibilitychange (SPEC §6.7; iOS needs >= 16.4). The engine's timestamp anchoring must keep the timer honest through brief backgrounding — verify on-device, don't assume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Screen stays on through a full 30-min session on the owner's phone.
- Backgrounding the tab for 10s and returning shows correct remaining time and interval, and the wake lock is re-acquired.
acceptance_criteria: screen stays on for a full 30-min session; 10s backgrounding preserves correct time/interval and re-acquires the lock

title: Home screen routine picker, zero-code routine add (SPEC §6.8)
description:
Home screen lists routines from data/routines/ with title, duration, equipment, exercise count; tap to start (SPEC §6.8). Static hosting has no directory listing, so the picker needs a precached routine index as DATA (e.g. data/routines/index.json, kept by the ft-mvp-ow6.1 validator or by hand per SCHEMA.md) — dropping in a routine file must never require touching app code. Leave a layout slot for history/streaks (ft-mvp-ow6.12); do not build it yet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a routine JSON (+ its index entry) makes it appear and run with zero app-code changes.
- Displayed metadata matches the routine file's contents.
acceptance_criteria: new routine JSON + index entry appears and runs with zero app-code changes; displayed metadata matches file
